parakeet: You know what's more telling than anger at God? The absence of heartbreak. You say you believe in a God who hears, who moves, who shows up, but when he doesn't, when the heavens stay silent, you're not devastated. And that's the clearest proof of all, perhaps. Because if you truly believed, if you sincerely thought the God of the universe loved you, listened to you, cared about your pain, his silence would crush you. But it doesn't. You just shrug and say it must not be his will. Or worse, you stop expecting anything at all. You're not crying anymore. You're not pacing the floor begging for clarity. You're not wrestling like Jacob or lamenting like David. You're just moving on, carrying the weight yourself and making peace with the quiet. Because deep down, you already know he's not going to show up. And if you're honest with yourself, the reason you're not heartbroken anymore, the reason your unanswered prayers don't wreck you like they used to, is because you've already let go. You just haven't said it out loud yet. If you don't pray daily, don't follow divine laws, don't hear from God, and don't live any differently than your atheist neighbor next door. What exactly do you believe in? What is it that you're holding on to? A label? A memory? A habit that makes you feel safe around people who still believe? Is it the word Christian or the idea of being a believer? Is it the comfort of belonging to something without having to wrestle with whether it's true? Whatever it is, let's be honest. It's probably not belief. It's identity, it's inherited language, it's cultural momentum. But what's the cost of keeping up the act? It perpetuates religious dominance. Systems that still shape laws, education, and human rights based on ancient myths. It fuels unnecessary guilt and shame. Burdens people carry for thoughts they didn't choose or desires they can't control. And it prevents real healing. Because you can't grow beyond something if you're too afraid to admit you're already past it. So maybe it's time to stop pretending. Not for me, but for you. You don't have to fear a hell to be a good person. You don't have to believe in a God to live with purpose. And you don't have to lie to yourself just to fit in. Let's just be honest. Most of us are already living without God. Maybe it's time to say it out loud.
